commits.edited_message:
knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals

Plain known-host entries are currently compared as text, so equivalent
expanded and compressed IPv6 literals do not match.

This change keeps the existing exact-string fast path and compares two
valid plain IPv6 literals by their 128-bit address. It also supports
bracketed IPv6 host-and-port entries while requiring the port suffix to
match exactly.

The legacy line parser also accepts the full 255-byte host field.

No DNS lookup is performed. Hostname matching and the CUSTOM and hashed
known-host paths remain unchanged.

Reported-by: Krisscut on github
Fixes #1398

Closes #2568

(cherry picked from commit dd47304a16597184d6147ac13d7f30ff4773ca44)

+++ b/src/knownhost.c
@@ -868,7 +868,7 @@ static int knownhost_line_legacy(LIBSSH2_KNOWNHOSTS *hosts,
             char hostbuf[256];
 
             /* make sure we do not overflow the buffer */
-            if(namelen >= sizeof(hostbuf) - 1)
+            if(namelen > 255)
                 return ssh2_err(hosts->session,
                                 LIBSSH2_ERROR_METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED,
                                 "Failed to parse known_hosts line "

coupling: The IPv6 known-host maintenance commit widens the legacy host-field limit to 255 bytes while its 256-byte temporary buffer still safely holds the terminating NUL. The later tidy-up reduces that temporary buffer to 255 bytes; on the original size-derived limit this is also safe. Together, the parser accepts a 255-byte host field and writes its terminator one byte beyond the 255-byte buffer. A repair must reconcile the host-field limit with the buffer capacity across the two changes.
